description: Personal views, locked views and protected fields in an SvGrid Base, in Svelte 5. A personal view is listed only for the person it belongs to, under My views. A locked view keeps its filter, sorts, groups, hidden fields and colors as saved, says who locked it, and still lets people edit records. A protected field takes edits only from the people it lists. A Signed in as switch shows each person's views, who may lock them, and who may set Priority.
keywords: svelte grid saved views per user

faq.question: How does the base know whose views to show?
faq.answer: From the signed-in person set with setCurrentUser. A view with personal set to their id shows for them only; with no one signed in, every view shows.

faq.question: What does a lock stop?
faq.answer: Changes to the view's settings: the Hide fields, Filter, Group, Sort, Color and row height buttons are off and nothing is saved into the view. A sort from a column header still works for the moment and the bar shows Reset. Records stay editable.

faq.question: Who can lock and unlock views?
faq.answer: Whoever the app allows: pass lockViews={false} to people who may not. In this demo Ana and Ben may, Cleo may not.

faq.question: Does a protected field stop writes to my database?
faq.answer: No. The browser follows fieldProps.editors for the person in front of it: the grid, the record view, a board stacked by the field and an import into the table leave the field alone. A base whose records live in a database still needs the server to refuse those writes.
